module purpose: neorv32_neoled accepts bus accesses to store serializer control and timing settings or to queue 34-bit frame entries into an internal FIFO, then consumes queued entries to drive a timed single-bit output on neoled_o. It also reports status through the bus response, raises irq_o from FIFO status, and exports clkgen_en_o from the local enable state.

use-case flows.value: store local control settings: enable, frame mode, strobe flag, clock select, interrupt condition select, total pulse length, and 0/1 high-time lengths
enqueue a frame entry into the transmit FIFO and, when data is available, select the first serializer phase for that entry
dequeue a FIFO entry, load payload and flags, shift bits, count pulse and strobe time, and drive the serial output waveform
generate an interrupt request from the enable bit and FIFO status according to the configured interrupt condition
return stored control settings and live FIFO/serializer status bits on the bus response data word
clear control registers, interrupt output, serializer state, counters, payload register, and serial output while rstn_i is low

conceptual assets.reasoning: The configure flow stores the enable bit in ctrl.enable at line 130. That stored value drives clkgen_en_o at line 160, clears the FIFO when low through tx_fifo.clear at line 193, gates irq_o at line 201, and is copied into serial.state(2) at line 231. Integrity matters because these control, operate, and report flows all depend on the stored enable state matching the written value; availability is also established because the register holds its value between writes and exports it on clkgen_en_o.

The configure flow stores ctrl.irq_conf at line 134. The report flow then uses that stored selector in irq_o generation: line 202 uses not tx_fifo.avail when ctrl.irq_conf is 0, and line 203 uses not tx_fifo.half when ctrl.irq_conf is 1. Integrity matters because the reported interrupt condition must match the configured selection; availability is established because the selector is retained between writes.

Control writes store ctrl.clk_prsc, ctrl.t_total, ctrl.t0_high, and ctrl.t1_high at lines 133 and 135-137. The serializer uses these settings to select a clkgen_i bit for serial.pulse_clk at line 225, to choose the current high-time in lines 261-263, to drop neoled_o when serial.pulse_cnt equals serial.t_high at lines 281-282, and to end bit or strobe periods when serial.pulse_cnt equals ctrl.t_total at lines 285-286 and 295-299. Integrity matters because output timing depends on these stored values; availability is established because the registers preserve the settings between writes.

Each data write forms a FIFO entry by concatenating ctrl.strobe, ctrl.mode, and the bus data into tx_fifo.wdata at line 192. When an entry is consumed, the serializer loads serial.sreg from tx_fifo.rdata(31 downto 0) at line 239, sets serial.mode and the initial bit count from tx_fifo.rdata(32) at lines 240-245, chooses the initial data-versus-strobe path from tx_fifo.rdata(33) at lines 248-251, and derives serial.next_bit from serial.sreg under serial.mode at line 318. Integrity matters because the operate flow must emit the intended payload with the intended per-frame flags; availability is established because the payload is held in serial.sreg while it is shifted at line 257.

conceptual assets.concept: Serializer progress and live timing state
conceptual assets.reasoning: The serial engine keeps its phase in serial.state at lines 231, 249, 251, 268, 271, 286, 305, and 311; decrements serial.bit_cnt at line 258; samples the selected tick into serial.pulse_clk at line 225; updates serial.pulse_cnt at lines 279, 296, and 299; stores the current bit high-time in serial.t_high at lines 261-263; and updates serial.strobe_cnt at line 297. These states are then tested at lines 265, 281, 285, 295, and 303 to change phase, finish a frame, or change the output level. Integrity matters because the operate flow depends on exact sequencing through these stored states; availability is established under the RTL-visible condition serial.pulse_clk = 1 at lines 278-299.

The report flow registers irq_o from ctrl.enable and FIFO status at lines 201-203: line 201 gates the request with ctrl.enable, and lines 202-203 select the status condition from tx_fifo.avail or tx_fifo.half. Integrity matters because the consumer of irq_o must receive exactly the request level defined by that expression; availability is established because the port is updated on each rising edge of clk_i when reset is inactive.

The operate flow drives neoled_o low on reset and idle/finish paths at lines 222, 236, 266, and 310, drives it high when another bit remains at line 270, and clears it when serial.pulse_cnt equals serial.t_high during the active pulse phase at lines 278-282. Integrity matters because this is the cross-boundary signal produced by the module's serializer; availability is established because the RTL drives the port in every serializer phase.
